title: Restore the rehearsal rescue
instructions: Read the complete passage first. Enter exactly one word in each gap to complete a natural collocation or fixed expression. Check all eight gaps before submitting.

parts.prompt: Gap 1: complete the fixed expression meaning “with little warning”: at short ___.

response.rationale: The established expression “at short notice” means with little time to prepare, matching the unexpected booking change.

parts.hint: The booking change gave the club very little time to prepare.
parts.correct_explanation: “At short notice” is the fixed expression for something announced with little warning.

parts.prompt: Gap 2: complete the expression meaning “accept responsibility for”: take ___ of.

response.rationale: “Take charge of” means assume responsibility for organising or controlling something, which is what Mei does with the schedule.

parts.hint: Mei becomes responsible for organising the changed schedule.
parts.correct_explanation: “Take charge of the new schedule” means accept responsibility for organising it.

parts.prompt: Gap 3: complete the expression meaning “watch carefully”: keep an ___ on.

response.rationale: The fixed expression “keep an eye on” means monitor something carefully, matching Arif's responsibility for the props and cables.

parts.hint: Arif monitors the equipment while Mei organises the schedule.
parts.correct_explanation: “Keep an eye on” means watch or monitor carefully.

parts.prompt: Gap 4: complete the expression describing an activity that stops: came to a ___.

response.rationale: Both “came to a halt” and “came to a stop” naturally describe the rehearsal ceasing when the sound system failed.

parts.hint: The sound failure caused the rehearsal to stop completely.
parts.correct_explanation: The rehearsal “came to a halt”; the equally natural expression “came to a stop” is also accepted.

parts.prompt: Gap 5: complete the expression meaning “very close to doing something”: on the ___ of.

response.rationale: “On the verge of”, “on the brink of” and “on the point of” can all mean very close to an action or event; each fits the team's near-cancellation.

parts.hint: The team nearly cancelled the scene but had not yet done so.
parts.correct_explanation: “On the verge of cancelling” means very close to cancelling; “brink” and “point” are approved natural equivalents here.

parts.prompt: Gap 6: complete the expression meaning “decided”: made up their ___.

response.rationale: The plural fixed expression “made up their minds” means the actors reached a decision to continue without recorded music.

parts.hint: The actors decide together to keep the scene and change how they perform it.
parts.correct_explanation: “Made up their minds” is the fixed expression meaning decided.

parts.prompt: Gap 7: complete the collocation describing an important contribution: played a crucial ___.

response.rationale: “Played a crucial role” and “played a crucial part” both describe the percussion group's important contribution to saving the scene.

parts.hint: The percussion group's contribution was essential to the revised performance.
parts.correct_explanation: The group “played a crucial role”; “played a crucial part” is also an approved natural collocation.

parts.prompt: Gap 8: complete the expression showing that the preparation changed the result: made all the ___.

response.rationale: The fixed expression “made all the difference” means the calm preparation was decisive in producing a successful scene.

parts.hint: Their preparation was the decisive reason the revised scene succeeded.
parts.correct_explanation: “Made all the difference” means had the decisive effect on the outcome.
